_readme: Curated by the architecture agent. Descriptions must be verifiable from code or ARCHITECTURE.md. Layer `row` orders bands top-to-bottom per side; package `order` orders nodes inside a row. architecture.json is generated - never hand-edit it.

server:main.description: Builds the FastAPI app: installs the error-envelope handlers and access-log redaction, then mounts the auth router, the scheduling API (app.api.install) and the agent router. Owns no logic of its own.
notes: GET /health is served here and is not in contracts/openapi.yaml (extractor http_issues: server_routes_not_in_contract).

server:agent.description: The LLM layer (ARCH §8): POST /agent/message, the manual tool-use turn loop, the static prompt and per-turn snapshot, strict tool schemas, in-memory staging and deterministic fallback narration. It stages mutations and asks the solver to propose; it never emits blocks or times. loop.py and router.py are the only importers of anthropic.
notes: Boundary pressure: agent/router.py imports app.api.busy, deps, outbox and views, while api/views.py imports app.agent.narration, so api and agent form a package-level cycle. No contract forbids it, because narration is allowed and router/loop are not imported from api.
agent/router.py also imports app.gcal.busy and app.gcal.errors directly (busy time for the in-turn solve).

external:anthropic.description: Anthropic Messages SDK (external). The llm-only-behind-agent-route contract forbids it in api, db, scheduler, auth and in agent.narration, staging and schemas, so only agent.loop and agent.router may import it.

server:api.description: REST routers per contracts/openapi.yaml (projects, preferences, exceptions, pins, blocks, plans, changesets), the thin gcal connection and Google sign-in routes, and the one REST staging path (api/staging.py). State changes go through app.db write paths; staged writes return the pending changeset (202). It must not import anthropic, agent.loop or agent.router.
notes: Composes auth and gcal for Google sign-in (api/google_signin.py), which is why auth itself is barred from orchestrating gcal.

server:auth.description: Accounts and sessions: Google and optional Apple sign-in, opaque bearer sessions (pure token/expiry logic in sessions.py), account deletion that revokes the Google grant, refresh-token encryption and the injectable clock. Must not import app.api, app.agent or gcal's orchestration modules; only gcal.client, errors and settings are allowed.
notes: auth and gcal form a package cycle: gcal/runtime.py, service.py and writeback.py import app.auth.clock, crypto and settings, while auth imports gcal.client, errors and settings. The contract comment in pyproject.toml records that a full auth -/-> gcal ban needs those modules moved first.

server:scheduler.description: Pure, deterministic solver (ARCH §4): pack(), verify(), the solver contract models and golden replay. It has no I/O, clock or env reads and imports nothing from agent, api, gcal or db (scheduler-purity). Every schedule comes from here.
notes: No logging, by design (pure). Failure is returned as data: Infeasibility in SolverOutput and verify() violations.

server:gcal.description: Google Calendar integration: OAuth with PKCE and stateless state, freeBusy busy time for solves, the app-owned calendar, the write-back outbox worker and ingest of edits made to our events in Google. Scopes are calendar.freebusy plus calendar.app.created only (gcal/settings.py), so other events' details never enter the system.

server:db.description: Persistence: SQLAlchemy models (db/models rolls up here), the session factory, the DB-to-solver contract mapping (solver_io.py) and the only write paths (persist_plan and apply_mutation in write_paths.py, plus agent_turns and the outbox). It imports scheduler for contract types and verify(), and never imports api or agent.
notes: No logging in db: failures surface as typed write-path exceptions that api/errors.py maps to the contract envelope.

server:errors.description: The app-wide error envelope {error: {code, message, details?}} (D12) and its handlers. It is a leaf and imports no app package.

server:log_redaction.description: A uvicorn access-log filter that strips the query string from GET /gcal/callback, so the OAuth code and state never reach logs. app.main installs it at import. It is a leaf.

ios:App.description: The composition root. AppModel builds the transport (mock or network), the typed client, the session store, auth state and app-wide observable state. AppConfig switches the whole app onto contract fixtures (-UseMockAPI).
notes: Every feature package references AppModel directly, so features reach the composition root instead of going only through Core/State.

ios:Features/Chat.description: The Chat tab: onboarding intake and mid-week conversation over POST /agent/message (ChatModel), project summary cards, the project edit sheet and the preferences step.

ios:Features/Timetable.description: Week and day timetable. TimetableModel loads the plan, pins, projects, preferences and exceptions and draws what the server says. Edits go out as staged PATCH /blocks writes whose changesets land in PendingChangesetStore; nothing is placed client-side.

ios:Features/Proposals.description: Proposal review for the current pending changeset: narration, infeasibility trade-offs, the diff view and the confirm/reject bar (design/diff-and-infeasibility.md).
notes: Features/Proposals and Features/Timetable form a cycle: review reuses the timetable grid views, and Timetable uses Proposals' RelaxationRequest and TradeOffContext.

ios:Features/Projects.description: The Projects tab: GET /projects in server order, with no client-side filtering, sorting or judging.

ios:Features/Onboarding.description: Onboarding: intro panels, Continue with Google sign-in (one consent for account, session and calendar) and the Google Calendar consent view.

ios:Features/Settings.description: Settings: Google Calendar connection, notifications, backend mode and sign-out, plus the revoked-calendar banner.

ios:Features/Notifications.description: The notification permission pre-prompt card, shown on the Week tab after the first week is confirmed.

ios:Core/Networking.description: The typed APIClient (one method per contract operationId), its URLSession implementation, the HTTPTransport seam (network vs mock), the SSE parser for the agent stream, JSON/RFC 3339 coding and APIError. Every server call goes through it.

ios:Core/State.description: App-wide observable state shared by features: tabs and navigation, the single PendingChangesetStore, the project directory and cards, the preferences form, the calendar connection and the timezone monitor.

ios:Core/Auth.description: AuthState (sign-in phases, sign-out, session revocation), nonce generation and the WebAuthenticationSession wrapper for the Google connect and sign-in flows.
notes: GcalWebAuthenticator references Mocks.MockWebAuthenticator behind the runtime AppConfig.usesMock flag rather than #if DEBUG, so the mock authenticator is compiled into release builds.

ios:Core/Storage.description: Keychain-backed session persistence (SessionStore, KeychainStore). The token is redacted from descriptions so it cannot reach logs.
notes: Layer inversion: SessionStore keys the Keychain service by App's AppConfig.Backend.

ios:Core/Notifications.description: Local notifications: the rolling 48-hour block-start window, 10-minute warnings, permission state and notification-response routing.
notes: Layer inversion: BlockNotificationPlanner uses PinJoin, which is declared in Features/Timetable/BlockPresentation.swift.
Core/Background and Core/Notifications form a cycle through DriftNotification and the notification copy and route types.

ios:Core/Background.description: The only path to BGTaskScheduler, plus the drift check: POST /gcal/sync, then a drift alert notification.

ios:Core/DesignSystem.description: Design tokens: colors, typography, spacing, radius and hit targets, motion, and the project palette assignment.

ios:Core/Formatting.description: Display formatting for spans and durations in the device time zone. It only formats and never computes or adjusts a schedule (CLAUDE.md rule 1).

ios:Models.description: Codable mirrors of the contracts/openapi.yaml schemas (Project, Changeset, WeekPlan, AgentEvent, Infeasibility and more). It is a leaf and references no other package.

ios:Mocks.description: The contract-fixture transport (MockTransport, enabled by -UseMockAPI), the DEBUG-only DemoTransport screenshot scenarios and MockWebAuthenticator. Lives in the app target.

notes.title: Two-layer agent boundary holds
notes.text: Only app.agent imports anthropic (loop.py, router.py). The solver imports none of agent, api, gcal or db, and every block row is written by db.write_paths.persist_plan. All three import-linter contracts are shown as red dashed 'must not depend' edges.

notes.title: Package cycles allowed by the contracts
notes.text: There are twelve two-package cycles. Four are between peers: api <-> agent, auth <-> gcal, Features/Proposals <-> Features/Timetable and Core/Background <-> Core/Notifications. The other eight all involve App, the composition root: App <-> Core/Storage and App <-> seven Features packages (Chat, Notifications, Onboarding, Projects, Proposals, Settings, Timetable), because App builds the feature views and the views reference AppModel directly (see 'Features skip Core/State'). None breaks a contract. They mark where the next change is most likely to tangle.

notes.title: iOS Core depends upward
notes.text: Core/Storage references App (AppConfig), Core/Notifications references Features/Timetable (PinJoin) and Core/Auth references Mocks (MockWebAuthenticator). Core is otherwise below Features.

notes.title: Heuristic limits
notes.text: Swift edges are inferred from top-level type names and skip comments and string literals. A type named only inside string interpolation is missed, and a project type that shared a name with an SDK type would be mis-attributed (the extractor lists ambiguous names). Contract violations are checked on direct imports only; lint-imports is authoritative for indirect chains.
